title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
key_facts: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed PostgreSQL 19; it was due in late September or early October and is now expected around 19 November.
Between eight and 10 significant features were dropped and postponed to PostgreSQL 20, next year's release.
Peter Eisentraut, a vice president at EDB and a leading PostgreSQL committer, attributed the reverts at least in part to LLM-assisted code review.

Some reverted features had significant architectural defects that would have been hard to fix quickly during beta; LLM review also surfaced a long tail of harmless edge-case issues, 'a list of forty defect reports'.
SQL Property Graph Queries (SQL/PGQ), part of the SQL standard since 2023, was among the features pulled; Tom Lane warned shipping it risked bugs unfixable until v20.
Eisentraut said the reverts were not due to vibe coding, as the technique was not available when most features were written.
PostgreSQL 19 will still include REPACK CONCURRENTLY; Eisentraut calls it 'a great release' that will be 'very robust'.
quote_evidence: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest iteration of the popular open source database, and held back an unusual number of features.

“The effective quality bar has been raised after the time the feature was written and committed. Unless the capabilities of LLM-assisted code review keep improving at the current rate, this situation should sort itself out for future development cycles,” Eisentraut said.
why_it_matters_hint: A very widely used open-source database ships several weeks late and without some planned features, as AI code review raises the quality bar.
event_date: Reported 16 Oct 2026; new release date around 19 Nov 2026
